speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: First drafted by our Republic's first Attorney-General, the late Prof Ahmad Ibrahim, AMLA has been regularly reviewed to ensure that it remains robust and continues to serve the needs of our local Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They have been central to our community ever since.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Since then, we have continued to engage community leaders, Muslim law practitioners and the general community on how to keep the Act current and effective.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Earlier this year, the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and its partner agencies hosted public consultations on the proposed amendments to the Act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We also benefited from a number of valuable ideas and suggestions, which we have incorporated into the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I would, therefore, like to take this opportunity to record my heartfelt thanks for the strong support from our Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We are united in our common goal to facilitate and improve the socio-religious life of the people and I can say with confidence that this Bill before us today is one by the community, for the community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Allow me to describe the key features of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: A strong marriage is the foundation for a strong family.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: When couples have strong relationships, they can better support each other and provide a loving and supportive home for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It has been encouraging to see good results of the work done thus far.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: While these are positive trends, the fact remains that minor marriages are more vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is against this background that I move to introduce two measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: First, new section 94A introduces mandatory participation in a marriage preparation programme for prescribed groups.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We will mandate in subsidiary legislation that minor couples do so first.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They will attend a pre-marriage programme approved by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), which aims to raise couples' awareness of the issues on marriage and to highlight available post-marriage support programmes and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: A minor couple must complete the programme together before the application for marriage is made.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The specialised programme for minor couples comprises two components.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: One, premarital consultations to help them better understand, clarify and address any concerns that they and their families may have about the marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Two, marriage education workshops for the minor couples to learn essential skills and knowledge to build a stable marriage and family.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Parents' involvement in premarital consultations, as well as parent education workshops to discuss their important supportive roles to the couple, are highly encouraged.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MSF will regularly review the programme to ensure that it remains relevant and useful to couples.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Second, under the new section 94B, parental consent will be required for a minor marriage, before the couple can make an application for solemnisation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Currently, only the consent of the wali, the lawful guardian for the marriage of a Muslim woman, is required.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Going forward, consent of the parents or the guardians of the party who is a minor will also be required.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There will be a list of the appropriate persons from whom consent must be sought in the various permutations, in the new Fourth Schedule.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This move, Madam, thus reinforces the importance of parents' or guardians' support in a minor marriage as their guidance, especially in the crucial initial years of the marriage, is critical to help younger couples build strong marriage foundations for a lifetime.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It must be noted that this consent is separate from the role of the wali in a marriage contract and does not supersede the wali's approval.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Once the parents' or guardians' consent is given, the application to solemnise the marriage may be made.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There may be instances where the consent of the appropriate person cannot be obtained because he or she is absent, inaccessible or under any severe disability or refuses to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Upon application by the couple, the Kadi, the person empowered to consider marriage applications and solemnise marriages, or his deputy, the Naib Kadi, must take due steps to satisfy himself that the consent of the person may be dispensed with.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Importantly, if the appropriate person refuses to give consent, the Kadi or Naib Kadi must first give that person an opportunity to show cause as to why his or her consent should not be dispensed with.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Kadi or Naib Kadi then has the responsibility of deciding if there are good grounds to proceed with the marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Divorce rates are relatively stable, but we must guard against any rise in divorces.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This Bill seeks to do two things to help.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: First, to require parties to attend a prescribed activity before commencement of divorce proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The new section 46A will primarily allow the Syariah Court to ensure that couples who seek a divorce first attend its flagship Marriage Counselling Programme (MCP), to see if the marriage can be saved.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: So, I am pleased to note that the non-attendance rate for MCP has only been about 10%.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The reasons for such non-attendance range from either parties being overseas, to no longer wanting to pursue a divorce.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: If the couple chooses to proceed with divorce, the Programme will be a platform for couples to discuss care and living arrangements for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Counsellors will be on hand to refer parties to specific programmes and services to address their other social needs, such as financial assistance or education support for their school-going children.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Next, new sections 43A and 43B seek to enable the Syariah Court to refer parties for further counselling or a family support programme at any stage of their divorce proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Where there is an issue of child custody or welfare, the Syariah Court may, where necessary, order a registered medical practitioner, psychologist, counsellor, social worker or mental health professional to examine and assess the child of the parties.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The assessment will be treated as expert evidence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Another option available to the Court is to appoint a child representative, where necessary, to represent the interests of a child.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Providing multiple expert but neutral layers will better protect the interests of the child amidst the divorce proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For most local Muslim marriages thus far, we are accustomed to have the Kadi or Naib Kadi present to witness the solemnisation ceremony by a wali.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: But a small number have had their marriage solemnised by their wali without the Kadi or Naib Kadi being present, before requesting that ROMM register the marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: During public consultations, there were serious discussions about the importance of better protecting parties to the marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The validity of the marriage will be impacted if the wrong wali has been appointed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The consequences are even more severe if there are children involved.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There is also no protection for parties of an invalid solemnisation if there is a transfer of assets or monies, or if one party is entering the marriage unwillingly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Having considered this matter carefully, we seek to amend section 95 of the Act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In so doing, the Kadi or Naib Kadi can verify that the appropriate wali has been invited to solemnise the marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Kadi or Naib Kadi can also direct the couple to go through the required processes set out in AMLA, where appropriate, such as the new requirements for minor marriages, as earlier mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Couples who refuse to comply will not be able to register their marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Next, for divorces, a new section 46B will allow, and therein encourage, men to apply as plaintiffs without first uttering the talak.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The talak is generally perceived to be final in effecting a divorce, once the Syariah Court clarifies and adjudges that it is valid.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, it should not and must not, be seen as a quick and convenient solution.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With this amendment, a husband who applies for divorce before uttering the talak can seek help with his marital woes and the Court may try to save the marriage by directing the couple to attend counselling.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: At the very least, the couple can have a safe space to discuss their post-divorce care arrangements for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Allow me to stress, Mdm Speaker, that this proposal does not affect the Muslim man's right to pronounce the talak if he still chooses to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, the talak should not and cannot be taken lightly and must only be uttered when all avenues to save the marriage have been exhausted.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This, Madam, accords with Islamic teachings that divorcing couples still have an obligation to treat each other fairly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We hope that Muslim husbands do not utter the talak frivolously and that couples seek appropriate help when they face marital woes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is thus best that the Court's resources are always used optimally, for the benefit of Muslims in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It would not be right for our Syariah Court to be used by those with few or no links to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This is for a period of at least three continuous years immediately preceding any application or before the commencement of any proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For Members' benefit, this provision is already present in the Women's Charter and we are following the same parameters.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This amount is close to 3% more, or about $90,000, compared to the previous year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Of the total disbursement, more than $1.52 million was channelled to 27 mosques to help fund upgrading projects and to support mosque programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: All these are a result of MUIS' management of the wakafs, which include careful planning to ensure maximisation of wakaf returns and attracting good tenants for wakaf properties.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: So, we must continue to ensure that the wakafs are well-managed so as to maximise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MUIS takes this responsibility very seriously and works closely with the trustees and those appointed to manage the wakaf, better known as mutawallis.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This is to provide greater clarity and transparency, as well as to allow for more timely interventions to uphold the good governance of wakafs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Current provisions enable MUIS to do so when it appears that the wakaf has been mismanaged, or if there have been no trustees appointed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, for these conditions to be met, the wakaf might already be in jeopardy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Additionally, if the trustee or mutawalli has failed to comply with further rules related to wakaf, or terms or conditions imposed by MUIS as part of the appointment, he or she can also be removed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This is important because MUIS has to ensure that the individuals appointed as trustees are qualified to manage the wakaf.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In some instances, MUIS saw disputes arise when trustees made unilateral appointments among themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Such trustee disputes, if left unchecked or unresolved, may adversely affect the management and upkeep of the wakaf.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For avoidance of doubt, the amended section 58 also specifies that a Court must not entertain or proceed with any proceedings relating to the appointment or removal of wakaf trustees and mutawallis.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is for parties to work with MUIS to address and resolve such matters.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This is consistent with a High Court decision last year that the High Court does not have subject matter jurisdiction over wakafs and that the power to remove or to appoint trustees lies solely with MUIS, as provided for by AMLA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MUIS has established a wakaf dispute resolution framework to help address any wakaf issues or disputes that may arise.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: On written application to MUIS, disputing parties can undergo a mediation process conducted by a MUIS-appointed Wakaf Dispute Resolution Committee, comprising parties with legal, Syariah, and/or counselling backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Should a settlement agreement not be achieved out of this mediation process, an inquiry process will be launched and the Committee will put up a recommendation to the MUIS Council for consideration.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We are here to help because we share the same goal, to support and help our community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, the sinking fund could be tapped on for carrying out building repairs or installation works, as well as the purchase of any property or asset to benefit the wakaf.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This was something that many trustees and mutawallis have asked for.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They see this measure as an important, long-term financial planning move for the continued viability and sustainability of the wakaf.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It has been observed that many of the trust deeds of older wakafs do not specifically address the long-term upkeep of the wakaf, including that of the creation of a sinking fund to maintain it for the long run.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Often, without sufficient reserves or savings set aside, the wakaf properties will fall into disrepair.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We do not want this sinking fund to become a burden to the wakafs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Hence, the proportion of income to be directed to the sinking fund will be decided in close consultation with the trustees and mutawallis, with their wakafs' resources and needs of their beneficiaries being topmost considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I would also like to stress, Madam, that MUIS cannot be expected to tap on community funds to save those wakaf properties that have fallen into disrepair, especially where such predicaments could easily have been avoided with some financial discipline.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Last but not least, Madam, allow me now to explain the need to better clarify the use of the MBMF in the Act, as currently covered in section 77 of AMLA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is already specified in AMLA that the MBMF can be used, and I quote, "for the purpose of building mosques in Singapore and for purposes connected therewith".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Naturally, this should include the purchase or lease of land, but we see the need to make it clear and transparent in the Act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Our full-time madrasahs are one of the key pillars for this, as they train our next generation of religious teachers, or asatizahs, to guide our community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With more funding sources, such as the MBMF, the Dana Madrasah, or Madrasah Fund, Wakaf Ilmu and other grants from MUIS, our madrasahs are less preoccupied with fundraising.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They have instead been able to improve the quality of education provided and concentrate more on teaching their students well.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: So, on this note, this Bill also specifies that the MBMF can be tapped on for building or maintenance works of any religious education premises or facilities, to ensure that our full-time madrasahs are sufficiently resourced to provide conducive learning spaces for their students.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: So, let us stay united in our commitment and resolve to develop a community of excellence, confident of its place in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: And I hope the House will join me in supporting these efforts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In general, I am supportive of these amendments but would like to seek greater clarity in some areas.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How does the Act compel the husband to file the divorce at the Syariah Court if there is pronouncement of talak outside the Syariah Court?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Next, the proposed amendments also seek to strengthen the trustee management of wakaf.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I support all these enhancements and would like to make some suggestions.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would the Ministry consider having term limits for the appointment of a mutawalli or having a process in place for a mutawalli to relinquish his position upon reaching a certain age limit?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is to ensure there is good governance and succession planning in the administration of the mosque.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I also support the establishment of a separate sinking fund for wakafs.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that this amendment is intended towards a reserve for the future upkeep and development of the wakaf, I feel it is important to set a minimum percentage of the wakaf's annual net income to ensure sufficient sinking funds are available to achieve the intended outcomes.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While the Bill allows the amount to be determined by the majlis after consulting the mutawalli of the wakaf, I would like to know whether the majlis has the final say on the percentage should there be any disagreement.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I would also like to iterate my support for the amendments to AMLA with regard to marriage and divorce.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In terms of marriage, I am in great support for greater responsibility to be placed in involving parents for children being married under the age of 21.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Marriage is a significant commitment with life-long impact on a person's life.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, parents and guardians should be empowered to play a more active role in such big decisions involving their children.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The pre-marriage counselling sessions can also go a long way in ensuring that young couples making this huge transition in their lives can do so in a better informed manner, particularly with regard to financial matters affecting the household which, as I understand, becomes a major cause of friction in several troubled marriages.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: On amendments in the Bill related to divorce, I welcome the move to adopt a more "child-centric" approach.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I have come across cases during my Meet-the-People sessions where children are affected when the Court orders the matrimonial home of the couple to be sold.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This could include making sure that the children have a proper home before the matrimonial home can be sold.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   In this day and age where it is practically impossible to control the flow of information, this has a significant impact on one's perception and interpretation of religious matters.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In our own Muslim community, it has led to some degree of polarisation when different segments insist on their approach or interpretation of Islam as the only one that is correct.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Complicating the matter further are the various extremist threats which are linked to religion.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In English): Madam, in conclusion, I believe that the amendments represent a right step forward in ensuring that the Muslim community can be clearer on means available to them, in a manner appropriate for the current context we see today.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I believe that with continued cooperation and constant learning, Muslim bodies and scholars, together with understandings of practices in their countries can help us make balanced decisions in line with the Muslim faith.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   The AMLA amendment Bill, being tabled is aimed at reinforcing Muslim institutions, enhancing the management of the Muslim community's assets and strengthening Muslim families by fine-tuning and improving the current processes and laws so that it corresponds to changing circumstances and is more up-to-date.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I believe that the changes made are intended to provide more benefits for the good of the Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I have a few questions that require clarifications and I would also like to put forth a few suggestions.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I understand this is meant for couples who are under the age of 21 years old.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It is a good and much welcomed measure so that young couples will be more informed about marital issues in order to be well prepared spiritually, mentally and psychologically before they enter marriage.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In that period of time, I had the opportunity to interact with many couples who attended marriage preparation courses, as well as married couples who were facing marital challenges.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Based on my experience, I believe that a marriage preparation course is necessary.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I believe that professionals and asatizahs who are involved in these two initiatives will wholeheartedly agree with my views.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It is important that every individual who wishes to get married is equipped with knowledge that will help their effort to build a harmonious and strong marriage.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: We all know that, for Muslim couples, marriage is an act of religious devotion and it is akin to building a mosque.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: If we want to perform our prayers, we must know the essential steps, the requirements, as well as things that could nullify and taint the prayers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: We must also seek knowledge on ways to refine our prayers and improve our concentration during prayers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The same goes for marriages – every couple must seek knowledge to ensure that their marriage is strong and stable.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: We have to recognise that marriage is an act of religious devotion and Muslim couples need to be equipped with knowledge to perform this act of religious devotion.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In relation to marriage preparation courses, I would like to suggest that the content of such courses focuses more on religious and spiritual aspects because, as I have said earlier, the fact remains that marriage is an act of religious devotion.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: When I was initially assigned as the educator for the marriage preparation programme "Bersama Mu" "With You" organised by the Ministry of Community Development, Youth and Sports in 2006, I attended a discussion session about the "Bersama Mu" programme before it was officially launched.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: During that session, amongst the feedback received from the professionals and the asatizahs was the absence or lack of spiritual and religious values in the course syllabus.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, after the discussion, the syllabus was improved by including the feedback that was received.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: If it is true, I hope that the Minister can clarify why this is so.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The next matter that I would like to touch on is the enhancement or provision of more powers to the Majlis or MUIS in the administration of Muslim institutions and assets.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As mentioned earlier in my speech, I concur that changing situations and circumstances may sometimes require administrative powers to be enhanced.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Clause 17 inserts a few new sections − 61(3), (4), (5) and (6).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: These newly introduced sections touch on enhanced powers given to the Majlis on the issue of financial control and administration of the wakaf and nazar am.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Clause 18(a) replaces section 74(3) with the new sections 74 (3A) and (3B) that will, among other things, give additional powers to the Majlis to remove, and to appoint a mutawalli in place of, or in addition to, a trustee of a mosque appointed under a written instrument.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As stated in this Bill, section 58(7) was introduced in accordance with a High Court case, that is, Mohamed Shariff Valibhoy and others vs Arif Valibhoy (2016).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Among the reasons given in support of the introduction of this section 58 (7) are that, and I quote, in English: (In English): "Parliament could not have intended for the trustee of a wakaf to have recourse to the Court upon enactment of AMLA because: one, concurrent jurisdiction over the trustee by the Majlis and the Court may lead to inconsistent decisions being issued by the Majlis and the Court on the same issue and different standards and different laws being applied by the Majlis and the Court; two, AMLA vested title to wakaf property administrative control over a wakaf solely in the Majlis; and three, section 63 limits the jurisdiction of the Court to issues that are directed to the Court by the Majlis." (In Malay): Madam, I understand the reason behind the intended changes.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, I feel that it is better that the Court option is still made available, so that those who wish to present their case in Court can still do so.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: At the same time, it is also true that power can be abused by anyone, whether they are the administrator or they are being administered, for whatever reasons.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In order to produce a community of excellence that is able and is respected, justice is one of the main pillars or thrusts.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The laws created are meant to provide benefits to everyone and not only for certain people.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: He upheld and, more importantly, exemplified justice as a leader and an administrator.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: While performing his duties as a Caliph, an incident happened where he found his lost armour in the possession of one of his people who was a Jew.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: He was sure that the armour was his.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Although he was a leader at that time, he did not use his position to force the armour to be returned to him.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In fact, he used the judicial system to settle the matter.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: To make a long story short, the judge decided in favour of the Jewish man with the justification that Sayidina Ali did not provide concrete evidence that the armour was his.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The Jewish man was truly impressed with the nature of justice portrayed by Sayidina Ali, to the point that the Jewish man admitted that the armour was not his, but that he had found it.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The Jewish man returned the armour to Sayidina Ali but was rejected because Sayidina Ali said that the justice system has ascertained and proved that he was not the owner of the armour and he must respect the judge's decision.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This incident caused the Jewish man to become impressed with the values of justice of an Islamic leader.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The island of Temasek was peaceful and tranquil, Its name was changed to Singapura, Act justly while in this world, For we will eventually answer to our Creator.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While I am not a Muslim myself, I wish, as an outsider and a friend of the community, to express my support for the Bill as it highlights three important traits of the Singapore Muslim community that I have come to admire and respect.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: First, the united spirit of the Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Singapore Muslim community has been contributing to MBMF since its inception as the Mosque Building Fund in 1975.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The contributions of the community have given rise to beautiful new and upgraded mosques, which add to our vibrant, multi-religious landscape, including the new Masjid Yusof Ishak, as well as the An Nur and Al-Khair Mosque, which serves the residents of Marsiling-Yew Tee GRC.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While these mosques primarily serve the socio-religious needs of the Singapore Muslim community, they have also been active players in inter-faith initiatives.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These include inviting other faith groups to the mosque to learn more about Islam, or just coming together to build bonds over an Iftar meal during the fasting month of Ramadan.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As an example, Al-Khair Mosque in Chua Chu Kang will be hosting the IRCC Appointment Ceremony this Saturday.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Masjid An Nur in Marsiling also hosted a networking tea for community leaders on the morning of Hari Raya Puasa itself.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I also note that our full-time madrasahs have also endeavoured to produce wise, grounded and competent asatizahs, or religious teachers, who are able to guide fellow Muslims in a diverse, multi-racial and multi-religious country, such as Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have seen leaders of the community, such as the Mufti, condemn extremist violence in other parts of the world and state firmly that these actions do not reflect the values of peace and understanding in Islam.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Religious Rehabilitation Group (RRG) has also done excellent work in advising the community to be discerning about what they read online and to seek counselling early for their friends or loved ones who may be exposed to extremist views.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: All these efforts are particularly important, especially when there are preachers out there who seek to de-stabilise societies with their problematic exclusivist and extremist views as well as skewed doctrines and ideology.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We are fortunate, therefore, to have an asatizah fraternity who appreciate Singapore's unique context and believe in the importance of preserving our social harmony.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The amendments to the Bill which clarify the use of the MBMF for mosque building and religious education should thus be supported.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The efforts will also lead towards the further strengthening of the institution of marriage.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These efforts show that the community is progressive and realistic in its challenges, and how it has always been keen to strengthen itself.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is this progressiveness and desire to improve that have seen so many positive trends on the social front, as were highlighted by the Minister earlier.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Third, to encapsulate the unity and progressiveness of the community is its resilience.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: All communities in Singapore have their unique challenges as well as issues.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Muslim community has never backed down from those challenges.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It has always been able to dig deep to find innovative solutions to challenges.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The creation of MBMF is just one of these, but so, too, are the various proposals in the Bill before us today.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Rules seek to strengthen the religious sector through better regulation of Islamic education centres and providers, as well as to provide a guide of conduct of the religious teachers, through a Code of Ethics for asatizahs.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: All these are intended to strengthen the resilience of the community against the threats of extremism.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Muslim community has always worked closely with the Government and the rest of the communities in Singapore to address some of these challenges.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It has been a partnership, not an adversarial or combative one.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Government must and will continue to stand ready to help, as it does for other communities as well.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And for all communities in Singapore, regardless of race or religion, we should all stay united as Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I reiterate my support for the proposals in this amendment Bill, which reflect a Singapore Muslim community that is open to diversity, progressive, modern and confident of its place in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore is a nation of multi-racial and religious beliefs.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Her citizens enjoy a high standard of living with peace and stability since more than 50 years ago.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The harmonious relations amongst the various races and ethnic groups which we enjoy is not at all by chance, but a deliberate effort and action amongst all, together with the Government, in forging understanding, tolerance and acceptance on the differences with regard to religion and practices which are deemed as sensitive.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: As a secular state, Singapore allows its citizens to make their choice of religious beliefs and practices freely and openly.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Muslims are assured, through the formation of AMLA, whose purpose is to supplement and harmonise the enactment of laws for Muslims with respect to Syariah and secular laws.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   I would like to wish a good afternoon to the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs and also to all parliamentary colleagues who are present.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Our country is a multiracial and multi-religious nation whose people have enjoyed a peaceful existence for over 50 years.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The stability and racial harmony that we all experience throughout the years did not appear and happen by chance.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, it is the result of a unified effort and understanding among all Singaporeans, as well as a Government that is attentive to matters concerning religion which can be quite complex and sensitive.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: As a secular nation, Singapore allows its people to choose their own faith and practise it.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, Muslim Singaporeans here are especially safeguarded with the establishment of AMLA that enables a part of the Syariah law to be administered, together with secular law, as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, issues like housing policies have changed several times to the point that it affects family unity and social problems like divorce have become more prevalent, and we should use all of these as a basis to constantly review the Act and its relevance to our daily lives.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Overall, the proposed amendments being tabled are quite encouraging and timely.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: However, there are certain aspects that raised my doubts and concern.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, I would like to touch on them and elaborate further.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The amendment to the Act under section 35 touches on divorce matters and aims to introduce requirements based on the period of residence.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: This amendment strengthens certain requirements and manages the issue of divorce from the perspective of foreign couples.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The amendment to the Act under section 46B touches on divorce matters which will allow a man to apply to the Syariah Court for the divorce process to commence after pronouncing the talak to his wife.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Such actions will make the situation clearer and complete the divorce process.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Although divorce is discouraged and undesirable, this kind of responsible action should be supported.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: However, not all divorce cases can be managed in a mature manner and end with a fair and equitable outcome.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, based on studies and feedback that I have obtained from Malay/Muslim social organisations, there are many divorce cases that end with the wives losing out.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Statistical information from random studies conducted by a VWO showed that, generally, men are the main cause of the problem of divorce within our community.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Is this amendment sufficient and able to solve the problem that I mentioned?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: What we should emphasise is that men should act fairly and responsibly when divorce and its subsequent processes commence.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: From the moment the talak is pronounced, men should be mandated as the party that commences the divorce and its subsequent processes until its completion.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The failure of men to comply with and fulfil this requirement can result in the Syariah Court taking appropriate action.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I, therefore, call for some groups and authorities, like MUIS, to study this matter more carefully.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I appeal to all those involved to pay close attention to this matter so that women and children who are affected can be protected and undergo this unfortunate process fairly.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The amendment to the Act under section 95 touches on matters regarding marriage by a wali who should be approved by a Kadi from MUIS, which includes the biological father of the bride.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I agree and can understand why this amendment is proposed, especially if the wali involved is not the biological father of the bride.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: On the other hand, imposing similar requirements on the biological father is not only viewed as illogical, but it can be considered as a violation of a father's rights in the marriage of his daughter.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, I appeal that this amendment be given further consideration.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The amendment to the Act under section 58 touches on the issue of wakaf management, which allows MUIS to manage disputes that may occur.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: This proposal hopes to resolve disputes in wakaf management quickly.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, I think that this is a good move and positive development.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I am confident that this will lead to a more proper and effective management of wakaf.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: One difficulty faced regarding wakaf management is that it is a personal issue.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, how much should the authority be involved in this matter?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: If the appointed mutawalli is unable to perform the duty and role that should be played, should the authorities intervene and resolve it?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Should a mutawalli be subject to specific requirements so that they are aware of their role and duty?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: What is a mutawalli expected to do when they take on this role?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The proposed amendments to section 74 are complex.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Without these amendments, the problem of wakaf mismanagement by a mutawalli who is unqualified and irresponsible will probably continue.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: It may even be more prevalent in the future if this issue is not managed immediately.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: On the other hand, the enforcement of this proposed amendment can be viewed as an intrusion into a private matter regarding wakaf management.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, how can we resolve this issue that appears simple, but is actually complex?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I feel that the best solution to this matter is through education.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Each mutawalli should be trained and taught about the responsibility and role that they should play.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Any failure on their part to deliver what is expected of them should result in intervention by the authorities.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that the concerns that I have shared can be resolved.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I also hope that the proposed amendments can help local Muslim Singaporeans overcome the problems that we are facing.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I just hope that we could do this more regularly, at smaller intervals, as we need to be in sync with the changes in national policies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Throughout the years, as our Muslim community evolved and our own Syariah law jurisprudence developed, various amendments have been made to AMLA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: There are also increasing numbers of Singaporean Muslims who are living or working overseas, thus bringing forth new considerations for the Act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Syariah law has always existed alongside other normative systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The adoption and implementation of Syariah law in countries with Muslim minority communities has always been an active topic of discussion and debate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What are some of the more pressing reasons for defaulters and how are we able to work with the couples involved to reduce the rate in future cases, especially as we are making certain practices compulsory with this new amendment?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Studying and understanding these reasons will be able to help us strategise so that our counsellors and community can anticipate the potential issues and address them in planning future interventions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How is this going to be executed and how will they assist couples who are in the process of divorce?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Pertaining to the Appeals Board, what and who are the composition of this board and based on what criteria are the members selected?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Perhaps, setting an average timeline or a range of timelines would be useful because the families tend to suffer during this waiting period.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Despite being time consuming, I do feel that this counselling is important as it can be the point where couples are made to realise the potential for reconciliation, thus saving their marriages and families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Pertaining to the sinking funds, are there certain set limits and criteria for this?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: There is mention of a "case-by-case" basis in the Bill, but are there other criteria which will be utilised and adopted with the new amended Act?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can the Minister also outline what the Dispute Resolution Framework for wakaf issues consist of and what it is going to entail.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: With the passing of the amendment Bill, I feel it would be an opportune time for MUIS and the community to embark on a public education discourse amongst the existing mutawallis, as well as the responsibilities of wakaf management, so that we can be as professional as possible in its execution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The Minister has elaborated earlier, but I would like to still enquire: are there specific guidelines which need to be adhered to with is new amendment?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can the Minister also elaborate on the "education component" of MBMF and what exactly it can be used for because there was mention of a Wakaf Ilmu and the Madrasah Fund?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But is it just going to be utilised for educational infrastructure or also eligible for educational programmes and software which involve education and teaching?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: On the Code of Ethics for asatizah, a list of guides and characteristics is given in the Annex to this Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can I ask the Minister how these assessments are going to be conducted and carried out?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are they going to be on an ad hoc basis, through their supervisors, mentors or feedback from the congregation, their students and peers, or are there formal appraisal processes that are going to be put in place?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This is timely and it is important for us to understand as these issues need to be treated with greater transparency, especially in today's climate and the numerous challenges in the Muslim world.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Section 46B also mentions an update on the payment of prescribed fees for the divorce to be registered.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: And I feel it should not be so low that the parties involved do not feel any pinch at all.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: (In Malay):   AMLA was tabled in Parliament in 1966 by Mr Othman Wok and Prof Ahmad Ibrahim.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It provides guidance and acts as a point of reference for Muslims in Singapore in the management of their affairs, as well as their family matters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: These issues include zakat, wakaf, family, faraidh and others.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: On the issue and principle of faraidh, due to the differences between Shi'ite and Sunni Muslims regarding inheritance matters, misunderstandings and confusion sometimes occur.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can the Minister clarify whether certain requests had to be done by some parties, and how it was done?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there any legal processes that should be followed by these parties and where can comprehensive advice be obtained on this matter, apart from visiting MUIS' website?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can the Minister also clarify about the usage of wasiyyah, who should obtain it and from where?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: For those who have adopted children or family members who have converted to Islam, what are the steps that they should take regarding this issue of faraidh?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: On strengthening Muslim families in Singapore, regarding marriage preparation courses, apart from minor couples, can every couple who want to marry undergo this course, because it has many benefits as well as resource sharing that these couples can use in their marriage?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What about those who went through a divorce and then remarried?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What are the measures taken to monitor the condition of the new marriages?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This problem is still apparent and a burden in our community and it is one of the most visible problems in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Before marriage, it is mandatory for teenage couples to obtain permission from their parents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What if they are orphans and have no other relatives?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is essential for us to understand how we can plan strategic measures to prevent adverse trends and manage high-risk marriages within our community together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Let us put them in practice as best as we can together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: (In English): The amendments must also be viewed in a balanced fashion, I feel.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is very timely for AMLA to be amended as it was last amended almost nine years ago.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is also very timely that in this rather historic Parliament sitting, probably Mdm Speaker's last as the Speaker of Parliament, that we are debating AMLA − a Bill that Mdm Speaker has spoken on before in this House as a parliamentarian during the last debate on the AMLA amendments in November 2008.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In Mdm Speaker's speech then, Madam spoke passionately about her support for the expanded use of the MBMF and the need to use part of the funds in helping dysfunctional or complex families in the community, beyond the traditional use of the funds in financing religious-related infrastructural developments for the community.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For this round of amendments to AMLA, I would like to speak on three areas: the use of the Mosque Building and MENDAKI Fund, or MBMF, Muslim marriages and the welfare of the child.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):     I support the amendments to AMLA.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the same time, I would also like to suggest that the funds for the MENDAKI component also be provisioned to organise and run job skills courses for, firstly, women, in order to help them return to work; secondly, those who are looking for jobs, and also, thirdly, those who are seeking a second chance, like ex-inmates and ex-drug offenders.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe that MENDAKI has already been proven successful in helping to improve the educational levels and academic achievements among our children in Primary, Secondary and post-Secondary schools.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have previously interacted with women who married their husbands as the second, third or fourth wife without registering their marriage with ROMM and the marriage was solemnised by their own father or relative.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is because their husband's first wife did not agree for the husband to marry again.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, this marriage is unregistered and there is no marriage certificate.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The choice to become a second or third wife is a personal matter that is permissible in Islam.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But I am concerned with the subsequent impact on the children who are born of this second or third wife.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Without any marriage registration and without a birth certificate, the child who is born will be similar to an illegitimate child, without a father.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will complicate processes like, first, getting an HDB flat for the mother and her child; second, registering the birth of that child and receiving related benefits like the Baby Bonus; third, matters relating to inheritance in the future; and fourth, when the child eventually gets married after he/she is old enough.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that with the amendments to section 95 and with the requirement for the presence of a Naib Kadi or Kadi in the solemnisation of the marriage, proper consideration will be made by the woman who wishes to get married as the second, third or fourth wife.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, Mdm Speaker, please allow me to continue my speech in English.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I agree that the application for divorce should not be made too easy or be allowed to be done frivolously.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In a marriage, there are bound to be disagreements or arguments and, sometimes, decisions can be made irrationally during such disagreements and in the heat of anger.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are too many instances where a married couple seeks divorce in the heat of anger and, because of egotism, they refuse to swallow their pride and retract that application for divorce, without sufficiently thinking through the effect of their break-up on their future and, more importantly, on their children, if they have any.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The addition of sections 43A and 43B is also timely.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: More than anything, the well-being of the child involved and affected by the divorce should be paramount.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Requiring the parents and child to attend the family support programme is important, so that the child is able to understand what is happening and what will happen upon the divorce of the parents.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also hope that through such family support programme, the parents who are seeking divorce will reconsider their decision and are able to see the effect their divorce may have on their child.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If divorce is inevitable, I hope the parents seeking divorce will be able to part amicably and provide adequate support and time towards their child, post-divorce.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The genesis of AMLA could be traced back to the time when Singapore was a British colony.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: During that period, there was an acknowledgement that whilst English law was to apply in Singapore, it needed to be appropriately modified to respect the religious beliefs and customs of the local inhabitants.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The enactment of the 1880 Mahomedan Muslim Ordinance reflected the official legislative recognition of the status of Muslim personal law.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This ordinance was replaced by the Muslim Ordinance and, subsequently, evolved into AMLA we see today.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe this historical perspective is relevant as it provides an insight as to why Muslims in Singapore are governed by a separate law in respect of certain matters like marriage and divorce.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The evolution of AMLA is, therefore, of great historical significance and, to me, personally, it reflects the beauty of the Singapore Story that embraces and respects the identity of the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The proposed further developments of AMLA tabled today which are intended to: one, reinforce existing Muslim institutions; two, enhance the management of Muslim assets, and three, strengthen Muslim families, are, therefore, greatly welcomed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Based on my observations of issues that I have come across in the course of my practice and my discussions with other lawyers, I would like to highlight two areas to be reviewed and included as amendments to AMLA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is indeed important for there to be a connecting factor before the Syariah Court exercises its jurisdiction.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Currently, in such situations where a divorce was granted by a court of competent jurisdiction overseas, the Syariah Court can make an order on nafkah iddah and mutaah, which are entitlements to the Muslim wife, but not an order on the division of matrimonial assets.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This decision is helpful in clarifying and confirming that parties involved in a Muslim divorce overseas have some recourse.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe though there is much value in resolving the root of the problem through legislation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In particular, it will allow for one Court − the Syariah Court − to deal holistically with all the ancillary matters, including nafkah iddah and mutaah.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I understand the Muslim Law Practice Committee of the Law Society had put up their recommendations and had made an extensive argument in respect of this matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I hope that these recommendations will be reviewed and appropriate amendments to AMLA be made.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The other issue which I would like to highlight relates to inheritance distribution in accordance to faraid principles.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The underlying spirit or rationale behind the faraid principles is actually one of fairness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The ones who get a larger share are the ones who are supposed to care for the more vulnerable beneficiaries within the family.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, in practice, often what is seen, is an assertion of rights and entitlement to the share of inheritance, without an appreciation of the duties and obligations towards the other beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: No determination or adjudication of rights, entitlements and obligations is done at the Syariah Court.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: If there is a dispute, the matter can be brought to the civil Courts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There is some dissatisfaction on the ground in respect of the current state of affairs, especially by those affected by the strict compliance of the principles and who do not seek the appropriate legal recourse.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I feel that there is also a lack of knowledge and understanding of the nuances of Islamic principles on this matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I appreciate that there is no simple solution.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There may be several approaches to take and each comes with it, different challenges.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: That would require appropriate manpower allocation and expertise.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I note that, currently, the civil Courts, applying Muslim law, has jurisdiction to deal with matters involving a Muslim estate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I also note the legal position that the determination of rights and interests is subject to the general law in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are, perhaps, other approaches in looking at provisions to allow Muslim dependants to claim against the estate or setting out detailed provisions in AMLA in relation to nuzriah or hibah.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I appreciate the complexity of the situation but there is a real need to address these concerns.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I, therefore, urge that these matters be reviewed and an appropriate resolution be put forth.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In this regard, I wish to add that fellow lawyers, in particular those who sit on the Muslim Law Practice Committee, have expressed their desire to continue to be involved in discussions with the Syariah Court and MUIS to work on further developments of Muslim law in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I hope the appropriate division in the Ministry will follow up with them so that more ideas can be generated through discourse and possible collaboration.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, I continue to hope changes and improvements in AMLA and also in the management of Muslim organisations in Singapore like MUIS and the Syariah Court could help make the lives of those in the Muslim community in Singapore better.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I agree that this is not an easy task for those organisations, especially in the context of modern life and with the presence of a variety of opinions about any issue.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This responsibility is best described by a Malay expression that advises us to handle delicate matters carefully and wisely to avoid making things worse.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Although it is hard, I think that we should possess the courage and wisdom to make certain decisions and take steps to prepare our community to face change and make improvements.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There has to be continuous education about Islamic principles and their application in the world today.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: On this matter, MUIS and, in particular, the MUIS Academy, have made wonderful efforts and these should be continued.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As society progresses, it is important to keep abreast with the times.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That means that the conventional methods of managing things must be reviewed and updated for even religious organisations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I rise in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But I would like to raise questions on some areas which I feel we can enhance further.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: MUIS has, over the years, contributed significantly to the welfare of the Muslim community with their policies and programmes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They have been presiding over the wakaf dispute resolutions and it is certainly a wise move to clarify and strengthen their responsibilities and powers with regard to this.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: No doubt, this will help to streamline the resolution process.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, despite these changes, what happens if MUIS, one day, for example, becomes a potential litigant itself?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Should there be a conflict of interest pertaining to MUIS, the prosecuted parties will certainly take issue with natural justice.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Moreover, giving MUIS absolute responsibility could be seen as a move that denies the public transparency and access to wakaf issues.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In fair and responsible governance, it is wise not to grant any statutory board or organisation absolute authority, no matter how capable or reputable they have proven to be.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is also why the High Court, independent of the Government and other Statutory Boards in Singapore, is required to preside over legal matters.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Aside from highlighting MUIS' authority in the management of wakaf matters, it would also be prudent to look into improving and standardising the management of wakafs across the country.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: MUIS could help to develop rules and policies relevant to the enhanced management and governance of wakafs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
