text: The various proposals to enhance the management of wakafs are to be welcomed, as accountability helps ensure that the wakaf is maintained and developed well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With clearer and better management policies, the frequency of conflicts would be reduced.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I would also propose that the relevant parties in a dispute should be granted a more public channel to voice their grievances under the existing wakaf dispute resolutions framework.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This will help to allay public concerns about transparency and accountability.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On a related note – I think the Minister mentioned it – I echo sentiments from the community to dedicate more resources from MBMF towards supporting madrasahs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Minister mentioned just now about section 77 specifying adequate resources in a more timely manner, for terrorist groups are abusing misinterpretations and misunderstanding towards religious texts to incite hatred and violence.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Religion remains a fundamental aspect of the lives of many young Muslims and madrasahs play an important role in training asatizah, who are potential powerful influencers with regard to religion and education matters.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   As with all developed societies, divorce is on the rise and the same goes for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Muslim marriages are not immune to this phenomenon as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Ultimately, children are the ones hardest hit in divorces.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is, therefore, the right move to implement mandatory counselling or family support programmes for couples with children at any stage of their divorce.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Engaging experts to assess and examine a child's well-being is a clear indication that the policy seeks to be child-centric.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But, while counselling and mediating sessions are good in theory, not all parties may be cooperative.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am pleased to note that an absence of one party at these counselling sessions will not result in a delay of the divorce proceedings.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is especially important when either party or children are at risk in cases of domestic violence.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My concern, however, is that without both party's attendance and cooperation in a divorce case, it may be difficult to implement some support programmes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, a parent who has de facto care of the children may deny access to the other party, even if mutual support for the best interest of the children is recommended.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Counselling only works if the relevant parties are willing to put their best efforts into it.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In addition, I note that there is no distinction of categories of persons required to undergo counselling and mediation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think a couple who has mutually and amicably decided to end their marriage due to personality conflicts, and a couple who is divorcing because one party has exhibited dangerous domestic violence tendencies, would require very different types of support for the involved parties and their children.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My point is that different needs arise from varying circumstances and also the external amount of support they have access to, such as their family members.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It would be more efficient to streamline the process by categorising, for instance, the types of conflicts and reasons for divorce and their possible needs before embarking on the counselling and support process.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Overseas divorces presided by a foreign Shariah court present another challenge as they could result in complex ancillary issues.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The application for asset division was then brought up to the High Court, which also turned down the application.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is a classic case whereby, if both the Singapore Syariah Court and High Court do not have jurisdiction, the husband can avoid having the matrimonial property rightfully divided.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This puts women in Muslim marriages in a vulnerable position.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I feel that it is important to do so.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Lastly, I support mandatory marriage counselling for all Muslim couples.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In fact, I think marriage counselling is very important for all couples, regardless of their religion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Divorce rates are on the rise and marriage and family expectations are vastly different from those of earlier generations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some advice from parents may be rendered obsolete due to the circumstances of the current generation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Moreover, Muslim marriages are a little different in the sense that laws pertaining to them are governed by the Syariah Court and the awareness may be lacking among some young Muslims.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The concern would be that mandatory marriage counselling may be deemed as coercive and it could be challenging to obtain their buy-in.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Nevertheless, I believe it is still ideal to have it.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Unfortunately, it is human nature to believe one does not require advice until they encounter a situation where they need help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Family Justice Act 2014 provides for the appointment of child representatives in the Family Courts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The amendment sought to be introduced by the current Bill seeks to follow this approach in the Syariah Courts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Often, in disputes between parents, the children are put in a position where they are forced to take sides.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may not be in the best interest of the child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The child representative scheme provides a good support system to already available mechanisms to ensure that the child's best interest is foremost in mind.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Family Justice Act 2014 as well as the proposed amendments sought to be introduced by the current Bill do not set out the precise roles of the child representatives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the context of the Family Justice Act, this is set out in the Family Justice Rules.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Similarly, I trust that subsidiary legislation on the proposed amendments, if accepted, will deal with the roles of the child representative through similar subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister confirm if this is the case?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also want to add that it will be useful to learn from the experiences of the Family Court in this regard.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, under section 45(5) of the Family Justice Act 2014, the child representative has some measure of protection from legal suits.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Clause 15(c) of the Bill similarly seeks to offer some protection to the child representative from legal proceedings in the carrying out of their work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is provided that the conditions set out therein are satisfied.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, the wording adopted for the conditions in the Family Justice Act 2014 and the proposed amendments in the current Bill differ.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some lawyers have raised this issue with me and wanted clarifications on whether there is a distinction to be drawn between the protection to be given to a child representative under the Family Justice Act 2014 and AMLA?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If no such distinction was intended, then the suggestion is that the wording of the Family Law Act 2014 be adopted.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After all, there is much sense in lifting protection only where the fraud and misconduct are attributed to the child representative.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should also mention that the same disparity in wording is also present in relation to the protection offered to medical practitioners, psychologists, social workers or mental health professionals in section 45(6) of the Family Justice Act 2014 and clause 15(c) of the current Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, may I propose that the wording in the Family Justice Act 2014 be adopted?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, similar to what fellow Member Saktiandi Supaat had mentioned earlier, sections 121A to 121G of the Women's Charter created jurisdiction for the Family Courts to deal with financial provisions consequential upon a divorce where the divorce was obtained overseas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In a recent case, the Syariah Courts have declined to exercise jurisdiction over such matters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In other words, where the divorce of a Muslim couple is finalised overseas, the Syariah Courts will not have jurisdiction to determine the division of matrimonial assets in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This becomes a problem when there is a divorce overseas and there are assets in Singapore which the overseas Court will not deal with.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This issue came up before the Singapore Courts in TMO vs TMO   SGCA 14.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In TMO, the husband applied for and obtained a divorce in the Johore courts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was done, apparently, without the knowledge of the wife.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The wife, having discovered this, later applied to the Singapore Syariah Courts for ancillary relief.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Syariah Court granted certain relief as it found that it had the requisite jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, it refused to exercise jurisdiction over the division of matrimonial assets on the basis that the divorce was not concluded in the Syariah Court in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ultimately, the issue relating to the division of the matrimonial assets would fall to the Family Courts who had jurisdiction to deal with the same, but would not apply Muslim law in determining the division.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This oddity that would follow is that all other issues would be dealt with in accordance with Muslim law, save for the issue of division of matrimonial property.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While the decision in TMO means that such a Muslim couple is not without recourse, the recourse provided may not be satisfactory from that couple's point of view.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is done while still having due regard to the beliefs and practices of our Muslim brothers and sisters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To this end, and the comments notwithstanding, Madam, this Bill can only improve the lives and interests of the Muslim community in Singapore and I stand in support of it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Their endorsement of our proposals to amend the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA) is, indeed, crucial.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Strong families are the foundation of a resilient nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But many of us would know, building a strong family requires constant effort, good communication and mutual understanding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These are but some of the important practices that our marriage preparation programmes seek to promote and encourage among couples.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: During the public consultations, there were also calls from the community for the marriage preparation programmes to be made mandatory for other couples, a point raised also by Mr Faisal Manap.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is similar to the approach adopted for minor marriages under the Women's Charter.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have several approved private partners onboard offering the Cinta Abadi marriage preparation programme for Muslim first marriages and this makes the programme accessible and convenient for all couples to attend.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, when we developed the Cinta Abadi programme, it was developed in consultation with MUIS, Syariah Court, Registry of Muslim Marriages and other community partners and they were based on the values of the religion and touches on the pillars of marriage in Islam.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For remarriages, a point raised by Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, there is a dedicated marriage preparation and enrichment programme for the couple and programmes for their children to help them adjust.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For couples who need more support, counselling, and even referral to relevant social assistance schemes and services are provided.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ultimately, it is about helping couples prepare for marriage and educating those who may not be aware of the importance and availability of such support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As I mentioned in my opening remarks, Madam, the Government will continue to study the landscape to assess if more needs to be done to support our couples.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we will start with minor couples and we will study further as to whether to extend it to other couples.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Rather, Madam, it seeks to ensure that the valid wali has been appointed to solemnise the marriage and once this is clear, the wali can proceed to solemnise the marriage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To answer Mr Zainal Sapari's query, the family support programmes available for divorcing couples are aimed at ensuring the best interests of children of divorcing parties.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, for couples with children below 21 years old living in a HDB flat, the Syariah Court will refer these cases to HDB for the couple to make informed and sustainable decisions on housing post-divorce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, the Syariah Court refers parents who have at least one child aged between six and 15 years old to PPIS As-Salaam Family Support Centre to participate in PPIS' "Children-in-Between" programme when necessary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The As-Salaam Support Centre is one of the four Divorce Support Specialist Agencies supported by MSF.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This programme equips parents with co-parenting skills to help reduce parental conflicts and thus minimise the impact of divorce on children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The programme also seeks to help the affected children build coping skills to deal with their parents' divorce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This one-time consultation session provided at the Syariah Court is known as "Parenting PACT", and is conducted by PPIS.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The session provides further resources and guidance on cooperative co-parenting skills and self-care strategies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It also provides information about the community support resources available post-divorce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is hoped that these programmes will give the strongest support possible to couples and their children in these difficult times.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They also complement the parenting plans that couples with children up to 21 years old may be required to submit, which essentially are post-divorce co-parenting and care arrangement plans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Counselling provides the safe space to discuss the implications of divorce and enables parties to receive proper guidance on self-care and post-divorce arrangements for the children of the marriage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For such cases, it is only to be expected that their divorce proceedings will take a longer time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat was concerned about parties in a divorce being non-cooperative.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If one party deliberately tries to stall proceedings, the Court has the option to order a stay in proceedings until the defaulting party attends the prescribed activity, or even order costs to be paid to the other party.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The conduct of parties often gives the Court insights into the parents' relationship with their child and, if there is a clear disinterest or lack of cooperation, such conduct could be relevant for the Court in its subsequent deliberations on custody and access orders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I would also like to assure Members that there is a "triage" system in place to determine the level of urgency that cases are accorded − irreconcilable divorce cases with a risk of domestic violence, for instance, will be expedited for the safety of the victim.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Louis Ng spoke of a Singaporean lady who obtained a divorce in Johor but faced difficulties in settling her divorce ancillary matters in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I believe they were referring to the case of TMO vs TMP (2016), which was brought to the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The High Court retains residual jurisdiction over matters which do not fall within the jurisdiction of the Syariah Court.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Therefore, parties to a foreign Muslim divorce are not stranded, as they can proceed to the civil Courts to claim financial relief, including an order for the division of matrimonial assets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As was done in this case, the Syariah Court will continue to make orders related to both nafkah iddah, which is the maintenance during the period which the divorced woman is forbidden by Muslim law to remarry, and mutaah, the consolatory gift upon divorce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will, therefore, continue to keep to current practices and laws.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In some ways, we ensure parity in approach, in that, if Singaporean parties had their marriage dissolved outside Singapore, there is a common forum in Singapore which is empowered to hear and determine parties' claims for other ancillary relief.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Such cases may often be more complex as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we will continue to monitor this situation and engage relevant agencies and stakeholders closely, including MinLaw and the Muslim Law Practice Committee of the Law Society of Singapore, or MLPC, with a view to better rationalise our processes and systems in future if necessary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First and foremost, there was no specific case that prompted these amendments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But allow me to reiterate some key points.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: By virtue of AMLA, it has always been MUIS' responsibility to administer all wakafs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Trustee management is critical to the management of the wakaf, because the accountability that comes with trusteeship helps ensure that the wakaf is maintained and developed well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Disputes related to trusteeship can be complicated, messy and potentially long-drawn.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the medium to long-term, the management of the wakaf can be adversely affected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is, therefore, MUIS' priority, in the interest of all wakaf beneficiaries, to ensure our wakafs are run well, so that they can generate the maximum returns and are sustainable in the long run.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We do not want the wakaf's resources to be drained by unnecessary legal fees.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This Committee is thus an expedient and prudent option, specially made available for our trustees and mutawallis who we value greatly for their contributions to the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Disputing parties who do not agree with the manner in which the MUIS Council reached its eventual decision can resort to judicial review by the Courts in appropriate circumstances.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But we would advise against this and would rather all parties come together for an amicable resolution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These amendments are intended to add greater transparency and clarity to MUIS' powers, such as in the grounds for removal, for the benefit of trustees and mutawallis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I wish to stress that these amendments on wakaf management should not be misinterpreted as an effort to give MUIS unfettered powers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They also help provide more self-sufficient avenues for the wakafs, through contributions to a sinking fund for the maintenance and upkeep of the wakaf.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We must laud the noble efforts and farsightedness of our community's early philanthropists in establishing the wakafs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We must also commend the good work of all the trustees and mutawallis who have looked after the wakafs well ever since.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we will continue to respect the traditions and objectives of the very trust deeds that gave life to these wakafs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They are as much a part of our history as they are important community institutions of today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The regular contributions from the community to MBMF over the years have made possible the building of new mosques and the upgrading of existing ones.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Maarof Mosque and Yusof Ishak Mosque are our newest mosques built with MBMF resources, with another in Tampines North set to be our 27th MBMF mosque.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the past year alone, we have seen six mosques upgraded, such as Al Muttaqin in Ang Mo Kio, Al-Khair mosque in Choa Chu Kang and, just recently, the Haji Muhammad Salleh mosque at Palmer Road in Shenton Way.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: When we brought this proposal to the public for consultation, the reception was positive, but there were similar concerns to what was aired today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There was recognition that good development of our madrasah students is critical to filling our "hardware", our institutions, with our strong "software".

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But there were also concerns as to whether this use of MBMF may compromise allocations in other areas, such as our mosques.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Ms Rahayu Mahzam raised two areas which were not included in this round of amendments to the Act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On Assoc Prof Fatimah and Ms Rahayu's query on having more amendments related to inheritance and nuzriah, allow me to state at the outset that my team and I recognise the need for a comprehensive review on these matters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I had said the same to the community leaders when I met them in March this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: More time is required to assess the changing landscape and study the implications of any such amendments to AMLA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS and MCCY are happy to work with our stakeholders, such as the Muslim Law Practice Committee of the Law Society of Singapore (MLPC) and the Muslim Financial Planning Association (MFPA), on this review to better serve the best interests of the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the meantime, members of the Muslim community are currently already able to make gifts during their lifetime or make nominations to benefit the parties that Assoc Prof Fatimah and Ms Rahayu mentioned, such as non-Muslim parents or adopted children, through their CPF and insurance policies or, separately, through a will.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I would highlight that MCCY and MUIS recently introduced subsidiary legislation through AMLA (Muslim Religious Schools) Rules 2016, to better support the asatizah fraternity, as well as our Islamic education centres and providers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Central to the Rules is the Code of Ethics, which all asatizah and Islamic education centres and providers are required to abide by.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The values within the Code are easily relatable to the wider community, such as recognising diverse opinions and schools of thought in Islam, not denigrating any racial or religious group and not advocating any idea that is likely to encourage extremism or violence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To answer Assoc Prof Fatimah's query, there are, indeed, processes in place to assess if an asatizah has breached the Code of Ethics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Asatizah Recognition Board will assess the matter and will subsequently put up a recommendation to MUIS on the next course of action.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Another aspect of the Rules is that all individuals who wish to teach or preach Islam must be recognised under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our asatizahs bear the heavy responsibility of providing the Singapore Muslim community with sound religious guidance amidst an increasingly diverse socio-religious landscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They are also our leaders in preventing problematic ideologies and practices from taking root.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The ARS thus seeks to raise the professionalism and quality of our asatizahs and ensure that they continue to be a key source of confidence for the community, one with strong professional qualifications and training to provide guidance on the practice of Islam in a modern, multi-religious and multi-racial society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS, together with its community partners, has been working closely and putting in much effort over the years to build the resilience of the Muslim community against threats and undesirable influences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These range from offering more customised religious education programmes and classes, to having outreach events and dialogues with parents and youths on complex, contemporary matters and providing counselling in "safe spaces" for those who require assistance or advice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They remind me of the equally warm reception we received during the public consultations, where many of our stakeholders and community leaders saw this review as a step in the right direction.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It was heartening that, from the very start, people saw this as an opportunity to work with the Government to strengthen our community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Many, indeed, came with valuable ideas and suggestions − some we have incorporated in this round of amendments, while some others we will continue to study with our partners to find the best way forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: What remains important is that we must continue working together, for we will always be stronger when we are united.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And it is this very spirit and confidence that will see us through, no matter what the challenges are, to an even brighter future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: (In Malay):   Mdm Speaker, next year, we will celebrate the 50th anniversary of the establishment of AMLA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This Act was drafted by Singapore's first Attorney-General, the late Prof Ahmad Ibrahim, to serve the socio-religious needs of the Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The last review on AMLA was done in 2008.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Almost a decade later, it is important to update this Act so that it stays relevant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am very grateful to the entire community for the support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Every suggestion is valuable and some of them have been included in the proposed amendments which are divided into three areas, namely, strengthening Muslim families, reinforcing Muslim institutions and enhancing the management of the Muslim community's assets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thanks to the determination and cooperation between families and community organisations, the marriage and divorce statistics of the community have shown improvement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Although the number of marriages has increased, marriages involving minor couples have decreased and the divorce rate has remained stable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This aims to provide a solid foundation to such couples in their early years in order to pave the way towards a lasting marriage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is important in order to ensure that the child's welfare is looked after in any divorce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, couples who wish to register their marriage must obtain written consent from the Kadi or the Naib Kadi.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Kadi or Naib Kadi must also be present to witness the solemnisation of the marriage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is to ensure that only the rightful wali is appointed so that the marriage is lawful in Islam.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, a husband is allowed and encouraged to apply for divorce before uttering the talak.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will allow the Syariah Court to help save the marriage through counselling.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We would like to stress that the utterance of talak is a last resort and should not be used frivolously.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Under section 58 in AMLA, MUIS is responsible for the administration of all wakaf properties in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is achieved due to careful planning by MUIS and close cooperation between the trustees and mutawalli or those appointed to manage the wakafs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In order to enhance capabilities in wakaf management, MUIS will be given powers to revoke the appointment of a wakaf trustee or administrator if there is any evidence of wrongdoing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This measure is important to ensure that the wakaf property is administered professionally and transparently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS will also be given powers to direct that a portion of the wakaf's income be transferred to a sinking fund to upgrade and develop the wakaf property.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This fund can also be used to build or conserve our full-time madrasahs so that they will have enough resources to provide a conducive learning environment for their students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Strong families form the pillar of a resilient society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Muslim institutions must be reinforced so that they can perform their responsibilities more effectively for the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The management of the community's assets must always be enhanced in order to continue providing benefits to the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Here, I would like to reply to Mr Faisal Manap's pantun or poem.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Singapore is a nation with dignity, Its people are wise and hardworking, It is entrusted upon each of us, To uphold justice as a shared responsibility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am grateful to everyone who was involved and who had contributed to every amendment to AMLA since the beginning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This includes representatives of Malay/Muslim organisations, professionals, members of the community and Members of this House who showed their concern, including Mdm Speaker.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am confident that Mdm Speaker will continue to give her strong support to our efforts to strengthen the Malay/Muslim community, in whatever capacity Madam may serve.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I hope that we can continue to work together to support this noble endeavour to build a Muslim Community of Excellence in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: (In English): I would like to close my speech once again by thanking everyone from the Muslim community for their support, not just for today's review of AMLA, but for all the past reviews of the Act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And this includes Mdm Speaker, who was always there with her wise counsel and valuable contributions to our discussions on past AMLA Bills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is, indeed, an admirable spirit and bond that our Muslim community share, united by a common purpose to do what is good and what is right for the people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I look forward, Madam, to your continued support in this endeavour, in whatever capacity you may be in in the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: I seek clarification from the hon Member, Mr Faisal Manap, on the meaning of the last two statements of his pantun, which is interpreted as a short poetry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Therefore, I would really like to understand a little bit deeper about the intended meaning and what is it exactly that the Member really has to say behind that pantun.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I believe that the pantun that I have mentioned is very straightforward and the meaning is already there, so I do not need to elaborate more.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Maybe the question by my colleague, Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, was not clear enough.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: It is insinuating that there might be certain aspects in the Bill which could lead to MUIS or Syariah Court to make unjust decisions.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: And I believe my pantun is very clear that we are all accountable to our almighty creator.
